title: 2021 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the Management of Valvular Heart Disease

definitions.Severe AS: AVA ≤1.0 cm², mean gradient ≥40 mmHg, Vmax ≥4.0 m/s
definitions.Low-flow Low-gradient severe AS: AVA ≤1.0 cm², mean gradient <40 mmHg with reduced or preserved LVEF
definitions.Severe MR (primary): EROA ≥40 mm², regurgitant volume ≥60 mL/beat, vena contracta ≥7 mm
definitions.Heart Valve Clinic: Dedicated multidisciplinary team for valve disease management
definitions.Valve Heart Team: Multidisciplinary team including cardiologist, cardiac surgeon, imaging specialist, anaesthesiologist

recommendations.text: AVR is indicated in symptomatic patients with severe AS.
For patients with severe symptomatic AS at high or prohibitive surgical risk, TAVR is recommended.
For patients with severe AS <75 years at low/intermediate surgical risk, SAVR is recommended; TAVR is an alternative if anatomy is favorable.
AVR (TAVR or SAVR) should be considered in asymptomatic severe AS with rapid progression, very severe AS (Vmax ≥5.5 m/s), or markedly elevated BNP.
MV surgery (repair preferred) is indicated in symptomatic severe primary MR with LVEF >30%.
MV repair is indicated in asymptomatic severe primary MR with LVEF ≤60% or LVESD ≥45 mm.
TEER (MitraClip) is recommended for severe secondary MR in patients with HF remaining symptomatic on GDMT meeting COAPT-like criteria.
Percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty is recommended for symptomatic severe MS (MVA ≤1.5 cm²) with favorable anatomy.
Anticoagulation with VKA (warfarin) is recommended for all patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis and AF.
All decisions about valve intervention should involve a Heart Valve Team.
Lifelong anticoagulation with VKA is recommended in patients with mechanical prostheses.
IE prophylaxis is recommended for high-risk patients (prosthetic valve, previous IE, cyanotic CHD) undergoing high-risk dental procedures.

pharmacotherapy.examples: Amoxicillin 2 g PO 30–60 min before; clindamycin 600 mg if penicillin-allergic

key_trials.name: PARTNER 3
key_trials.finding: TAVR non-inferior to SAVR at 2 years in low-risk severe AS

key_trials.name: COAPT
key_trials.finding: 47% reduction in HF hospitalization; 29% reduction in mortality vs GDMT

key_trials.name: AVATAR
key_trials.drug: early AVR in asymptomatic severe AS
key_trials.finding: Early AVR reduced CV events vs watchful waiting

key_trials.name: RECOVERY
key_trials.finding: Early surgery reduced mortality vs conservative management in asymptomatic severe AS
